## Why Estimates of the 1906 Earthquake’s Magnitude Differ

One team examined seismic recordings from 96 observatories, then digitized and modeled usable data from 12. Its analysis suggested a surface-wave magnitude of 7.7.

A USGS team took a different approach, re-evaluating geodetic measurements made before and after the earthquake. The method used ground deformation reflected in angles and distances between benchmarks, producing an estimate of 7.9.

The two estimates differ: seismic and geodetic methods of estimating earthquake size can yield different results.
